These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. - **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.

- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).

   park it wears *is* the in-review state and the failure park *is* the report (which
   is why `--pr` is still required on an approval — a park nobody can act on is not
   a park). The standing status is also what stops the next scheduler run adopting
   the same issue again; clearing it is a person's decision, made after reading what
   the run said. Only an item filed under the older shadow model writes back to a
   different issue, and the command does that too.

   Only `task:status:needs-human-failure` (and a park whose kind cannot be decoded) holds the
   task's lane — while one is open the generator files no further occurrence of
   this task. The other three wait for their human while the schedule carries on,
   so leaving one open costs nobody but the person it names.

   The `claudinite-task-exec` record goes onto the item, in the same comment, and
   the command writes it — Actions logs expire and the item does not, so the item
   is where a record has to live. Nothing here is yours to print by hand.

7. **Capture this session before you end it.** Last step, after the item is
   converged, and run it whichever way step 6 went:

   ```bash
   CLAUDINITE_SESSION_ISSUE=<n> node <engine>/hooks/session-end-command.mjs
   ```

   That runner invokes whatever session-end steps this repo's declared packs
   contribute; it knows nothing about what any of them do, and a repo that
   contributes none does nothing. Nobody is sitting in front of this session, so it
   ends by having its container reclaimed — precisely the ending that fires no
   `SessionEnd` hook. Left to the hook, every unattended run would leave no record
   of itself anywhere: not of the skills it loaded, not of the checks that caught
   something, not of how the work actually went, and not of the record you just
   printed. `CLAUDINITE_SESSION_ISSUE` is what files those logs under the item that
   ran, rather than under nothing.

   It cannot fail your run — the item is already converged and this changes nothing
   on GitHub. If it reports an error, **say so plainly in your final message** and
   end anyway.

## The one standing bound

You execute **this one item and nothing else**. Never list other work items,
never sweep the queue, never act on a second issue in this session — however
obviously stuck another one looks. Recovery is code that runs elsewhere, and a
session that helps out is how one item becomes three duplicate PRs.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

The worker resolves its flows against a **fresh canon clone at HEAD**, not the member's own mount:

```js
git(['clone', '--depth', '1', CANON_URL, tmp]);
const load = async (rel) => import(pathToFileURL(join(tmp, rel)).href);
```

```
.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-lifecycle/tasks/update/worker.mjs
```

1	// The claudinite-fleet-sheepdog pack's fleet CONFIG reader — the one parser for the enforcer repo's
2	// `claudinite-fleet-sheepdog` pack entry.
3	//
4	// It lives at the pack root, not inside a task, because EVERY sweep reads the same
5	// entry: the roster sweep (tasks/fleet-roster/) needs `owner` and `exclude` for its
6	// coverage half plus `canonRepo` for its freshness half, and the
7	// pack-seed sweep (tasks/fleet-pack-seeds/) those plus `packSeeds`. A
8	// second reader would be a second place for the owner/exclude semantics to drift —
9	// and this is what the file-placement skill calls lifting a shared dependency to the
10	// nearest common ancestor: distance 2 from each task instead of one task reaching
11	// into the other's folder.
12	
13	import { canonicalPackId } from '../../engine/pack_loader/renamed-packs.mjs';
14	
15	// The enforcer repo's .claudinite-settings.json carries, on this pack's entry:
16	//   { "id": "claudinite-fleet-sheepdog", "config": { owner: "missingbulb", kind: "user", exclude: ["owner/repo", ...],
17	//                                   canonRepo: "missingbulb/Claudinite",
18	//                                   packSeeds: [{ id: "<a pack>", config: { ... } }] } }
19	// owner is who to cover (default: the enforcer repo's own owner); exclude is the repos
20	// deliberately kept out (a full owner/name each, lowercased). canonRepo is the
21	// freshness sweep's one knob and packSeeds the pack-seed sweep's one, and both
22	// default, so an existing config keeps working untouched. Callers read the
23	// home repo's file raw (fetched over the API, no
24	// engine on hand), so this resolves the entry itself — legacy top-level
25	// packConfig.sheepdog stays readable underneath until the `pack-entry-config` baseline
26	// migration retires (drop the fallback then). A missing config is an unreadable
27	// config: throw — absence is not consent to cover everything.
28	//
29	// BOTH SPELLINGS OF THE ID RESOLVE. The declaration this reads is the enforcer's own
30	// file as it stands on disk, which converges onto today's id on its own schedule; the
31	// legacy `packConfig` key is a member-written key that never converges at all. An
32	// enforcer whose declaration has not caught up must still cover its fleet, so the
33	// entry is matched through the engine's rename map and the old `packConfig` key is
34	// read as it was written.
35	export function parseSheepdogConfig(cfg, home) {
36	  const entry = (Array.isArray(cfg?.packs) ? cfg.packs : [])
37	    .find((e) => typeof e?.id === 'string' && canonicalPackId(e.id) === 'claudinite-fleet-sheepdog');
38	  const sd = entry?.config ?? cfg?.packConfig?.['claudinite-fleet-sheepdog'] ?? cfg?.packConfig?.sheepdog;
39	  if (!sd || typeof sd !== 'object') {
40	    throw new Error(`the fleet-enforcer repo ${home} declares no claudinite-fleet-sheepdog config { owner, exclude } (on the pack entry or legacy packConfig) — nothing to cover`);
41	  }
42	  const owner = String(sd.owner ?? home.split('/')[0]).toLowerCase();
43	  const exclude = new Set((Array.isArray(sd.exclude) ? sd.exclude : []).map((s) => String(s).toLowerCase()));
44	  // Claudinite's own repo — where the engine and pack versions a member is measured
45	  // against are read from, and what its stamped ref is checked to be on the trunk of.
46	  // Named rather than inferred from the ref, because a ref tells you nothing about
47	  // where it came from; defaulted so no existing claudinite-fleet-sheepdog config has to change.
48	  const canonRepo = String(sd.canonRepo ?? `${owner}/Claudinite`);
49	  // The pack declarations this fleet wants in every member — each `{ id, config? }`,
50	  // seeded by the pack-seed sweep. THE ENFORCER NAMES NO PACK: this list is the whole
51	  // vocabulary, supplied by the fleet that declares this pack, because the packs a
52	  // fleet standardizes on (and the parameters only the fleet knows — where its
53	  // people's files live, which repo holds something shared) are its business and not
54	  // this pack's. Absent or malformed is an empty list: a fleet asking its members to
55	  // declare nothing in particular is an ordinary fleet.
56	  const packSeeds = (Array.isArray(sd.packSeeds) ? sd.packSeeds : [])
57	    .filter((seed) => seed && typeof seed === 'object' && typeof seed.id === 'string' && seed.id.trim())
58	    .map((seed) => ({
59	      id: seed.id.trim(),
60	      ...(seed.config !== null && typeof seed.config === 'object' && !Array.isArray(seed.config) ? { config: seed.config } : {}),
61	    }));
62	  return { owner, exclude, canonRepo, packSeeds };
63	}

{"number":1352,"title":"Delete the engine/scheduler shims, and repoint the worker off the updates/ ones","body":"L4, **split in two**. Supersedes #1329, which treated the two shim trees as one step. They have different retirement gates and cannot go together — and merging #1329 as written would have wedged all 13 members on their next update run.

## `engine/scheduler/` — gone

Safe now: nothing in the canon imports it (only tests reference it), and it is named by member **workflow** files, which all 13 now point at the pack mount.

With it go the vendor set's two temporary rules — the engine walk that shipped the shims only where the pack shipped, and the tolerance that shipped `claudinite-tasks` whether or not a member declared it (every stamp carries it now). The reviewed barrier exception that let `engine/scheduler/` name a pack goes too, and `scheduler-workflow-shape` stops accepting the engine path as a scheduler entry.

## `updates/` — kept, one more cycle

**This is the half #1329 got wrong.** The worker resolves its flows against a *fresh canon clone at HEAD*, not its own mount:

```js
git(['clone', '--depth', '1', CANON_URL, tmp]);
const load = async (rel) => import(pathToFileURL(join(tmp, rel)).href);
const { engineUpdate } = await load('updates/engine-update.mjs');
```

So the surface a member calls is whatever **its** vendored worker names — and every member vendored a worker naming `updates/*` earlier today. Deleting the tree fails every member's next update at module resolution, unrepairable, because the repair *is* the update. #1329 deletes it without repointing those calls, despite its body claiming otherwise.

This repoints the worker at `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/*`, so the next converge fields a worker that no longer needs the shim. The tree comes out in a follow-up, gated on reading the members' vendored workers — never a date.

`install.test.mjs` now pins **both** surfaces, because both are fielded. #1329 rewrote it to pin only the new one, which would have switched off the single test guarding this.

## The 21 dangling references, resolved by kind

Deleting `engine/scheduler/` makes 21 references dangle. They are not all the same thing:

| Count | What they are | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | Fixture **member workflows** in `vendoring/rehearsal/` | Repointed to the pack, exactly as the real fleet was today |
| 8 | **Legacy wire literals** | Moved to one shared module beside a single waiver |
| 2 | Incidental fixture paths | Repointed |
| 1 | A past-incident narrative in a comment | Trimmed so it reads without spelling a path |

The eight are the interesting ones. A work item minted before the move still carries `engine/scheduler/` in its machine block, and `BUILT_IN_PATH_RE` accepts that root **permanently** — its own comment says why: it is a validator, so dropping either root rejects that half of the ad-hoc request lane outright. Those literals are protocol a decoder must keep understanding, not pointers to files that must exist. `reference-integrity` cannot tell the difference, so they now live in `packs/claudinite-tasks/test/legacy-protocol.mjs` with one accept entry against it — rather than five waivers scattered across the tests that exercise the decode, which is also the shared-constant rule applied to a literal that was copied five times.

The `tick.mjs` entry alternation is deliberately **left alone**: that is #974's migration, with its own gate and its own test file. Retiring two unrelated tolerances in one PR is how a gate gets missed.

## Verification

Full suite 2734 passing, `check_the_work` clean, `check_the_world` 0 blocking. The advisory count drops 142 → 88 — the `file-placement` advisories the shim files were carrying.

```
engine/scheduler/            deleted
packs/claudinite-lifecycle/  the worker names the flows' real home; the cron check drops the engine entry path
packs/claudinite-tasks/      legacy wire literals get one home
packs/claudinite-canary-repo/ a README link followed the move
vendoring/                   the shim gating and the undeclared-pack tolerance come out; fixture workflows repointed
.claudinite-settings.json    the engine/scheduler barrier exception out, one reference-integrity waiver in
```
